messages:
maria: Heads up — several customers (acme, foodly) opened tickets reporting repeated 504s and long tail timeouts on hosted text-gen starting ~12:30 UTC. Tickets 9874, 9902. Request p95/p99 spiked. @oncall-bot can you share the pool metrics?

oncall-bot: Alert: RequestQueueDepth > 90% for hosted-us-east-1 gpu-pool-3 for 3m. Continuous-batcher backlog growing. Current queued_requests=2784, dequeue_rate down 65%. Dash: https://dash.redwood/s/gpu-pool-3/queue

ben: Seeing enqueue_latency climb and many requests stuck in "waiting_for_batch" state. Sample logs from gateway:
```
2026-03-15T12:29:41Z gw1 hydra: enqueue delay=1220ms tenant=acme req_id=abc123 state=waiting_for_batch
2026-03-15T12:29:42Z gw1 hydra: enqueue delay=1580ms tenant=foodly req_id=def456 state=waiting_for_batch
2026-03-15T12:29:43Z gw1 hydra: dequeue success req_id=ghi789 batch_size=32 exec_ms=2100
```

sree: Any auth/billing errors or 429s? or is it pure queue saturation? Also paste a curl sample repro if you have one.

maria: No 4xxs from customers, mostly 504/gateway timeouts. Here's a quick curl that's hitting the timeout consistently against the hosted API (same tenant):
```
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-xxx' -d '{"model":"rw-text-6B","prompt":"hello","max_tokens":2000,"stream":false}' https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate 
# -> HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout after ~12s
```

jordan: Repro notes: long sequences + stream:false are causing requests to sit in batcher longer because aggregator waits to fill target batch_size. Our continuous-batcher defaults: target_batch=32, max_wait=50ms. When many long-seq requests arrive they occupy execution slots for multiple seconds so the queue tail starves. Quick repro script (simplified):
```python
# hammer long seqs
for _ in range(200):
  requests.post(API, json={'model':'rw-text-6B','prompt':'x'*4000,'max_tokens':1800,'stream':False})
```

ben: Took action: temporarily increased queue_depth_limit for gpu-pool-3 from 2k -> 10k and enabled an early-reject threshold to avoid 100% saturation. Early metrics: queued_requests fell to ~900 but we observed memory headroom warnings on some thin nodes. Proceeding cautiously.

maria: Customer update: after routing heavy tenants off the shared pool to a smaller quantized variant and applying early-reject, error rate dropped ~70% for now. Still seeing P99 tail ~8s on some hosts.

sree: Hypothesis: the aggregator is delaying flushes waiting for batch fill; if we lower max_wait (batch_timeout) from 50ms -> 10ms we should reduce tail latency at cost of some throughput. Can we canary that config? Also check KVCache occupancy — long sequences increase KV lifetime and may reduce throughput.

jordan: Canary results: flipped batch_timeout=10ms on 2 nodes in pool. p95 reduced from 2.1s -> 1.3s, p99 reduced from ~8s -> ~3.5s, but throughput dropped ~8% under the same load. KVCacheMiss rate remained similar, suggests the primary issue was batching latency rather than cache thrash. Logs from canary:
```
2026-03-15T13:02:12Z node-canary1 batcher: flush(reason=timeout) batch_size=5 elapsed_ms=12
2026-03-15T13:02:13Z node-canary1 serve: exec_ms=1020 req_id=zzz111
```

maria: Good. Next steps: expand canary to 20% of pool, push a shorter batch_timeout as a mitigation for hot tenants, and add a runbook entry (continuous-batcher tail) for support. I'll open an incident page and link the customer tickets for follow-up.

ben: Also recommend adding a per-tenant batch_size cap and routing heavy long-seq tenants to dedicated/different variants to avoid shared-pool tail risk.

sree: Agreed. I'll draft a short runbook snippet: detection thresholds, immediate mitigations (route tenant, lower batch_timeout, early-reject), and longer-term fixes (adaptive batching by seq-length, per-tenant isolation).

maria: Thanks team. Support, please update ACME/FOODLY tickets with: temporary mitigation applied, ETA for broader rollout ~1h, and request any logs/requests sample from customers if problems persist. :thumbsup:
